title: SRE cross-functional launch kit — SLO operationalization Q3 2025
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic, cross-functional launch kit for operationalizing service-level objectives (SLOs) across product, platform, and SRE teams. It collects the minimum set of artifacts, milestones, and gating checks needed to move from SLO design to live enforcement and reporting.

Context and scope:
- Scope: Redwood-hosted APIs and Dedicated inference control plane routes used by customers (hosted-api and dedicated namespaces). Excludes private-deploy on-prem installations for this first wave.
- Objective: Ship standardized SLOs (latency p99/p95, availability, error-rate) with dashboards, alerts, error-budget policies, and documented runbooks so teams can safely operate and iterate.

High-level objectives (success criteria):
1) Dashboards live for each service with SLOs and error budget burn visible (95% coverage of routes by end of Q3).
2) Automated alerts for accelerated budget burn and sustained breaches (pagereduction target: 30% noise reduction vs ad hoc alerts).
3) Documented rollback and fallback policies per route, integrated into deployment rollouts and canary gating.
4) On-call playbooks and runbooks added to the knowledge base; SRE-led training for product owners completed.
5) SLO gating integrated into CI/CD for canary promotion where applicable.

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- SRE (lead): Maya Chen — program owner, dashboard templates, alert tuning, runbook consolidation.
- Platform infra: Lars Berg — instrumentation hooks, metrics schema changes, metric exporters.
- Serving runtime (engine): Diego Ramirez — latency measurement points, compat hooks for quantized models.
- Product & PM: Sofia Patel — SLO definitions, customer-facing expectations, product rollout coordination.
- Observability & Analytics: Imani Okafor — cost of dashboards, long-term retention plan, anomaly detectors.
- Solutions/CS: Rohan Mehta — customer comms for any visible changes and error budget policies.

Minimum deliverables per service/route (checklist):
- SLO definition file (YAML) with objective, window, and SLIs.
- Metric instrumentation validated (histograms for latency, counters for success/failure).
- Grafana dashboard tile and pre-built alert query.
- Error budget policy doc: escalation thresholds, keeper steps, stakeholder contacts.
- Runbook: step-by-step mitigation and rollback procedures for SLO breach.
- CI gating config (canary gating rule) if route supports canary.

Timeline and milestones (Q3 2025):
- Week 1 (Jul 7–11): Kickoff, finalize SLO templates and metric names.
- Week 2–3 (Jul 14–25): Instrumentation changes merged for first 6 critical routes.
- Week 4 (Jul 28–Aug 1): Dashboards prototype + alert rules for pilot routes.
- Week 6 (Aug 11–15): Pilot canary gating integrated for two product routes; runbook dry-run.
- Week 8 (Aug 25–29): Cross-team tabletop incident with simulated error-budget burn.
- Week 10 (Sep 8–12): Ramp to 50% of priority routes; training sessions for product owners.
- Week 12 (Sep 22–26): Post-launch review, noise analysis, and policy adjustments.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 — Design & agreement: finalize SLO semantics, percentiles, and acceptable windows.
Phase 1 — Pilot (3 routes): validate instrumentation and visualization, tune alerts.
Phase 2 — Expansion (next 10–15 routes): operationalize templates, handoff to service owners.
Phase 3 — Everywhere else: policy enforcement and CI gating on supported services.

SLOs and suggested baselines (starting point for discussion):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for customer-facing APIs.
- Latency: 95th percentile < 200ms, 99th percentile < 600ms for small payload text generation endpoints (subject to model and sequence-length zoning).
- Error rate: < 0.2% for 5xx class failures aggregated monthly.
Notes: these baselines must be adjusted per service class and customer tier (dedicated vs hosted).

Error budget policy (example):
- Green: < 50% budget used for window — monitor, no action.
- Yellow: 50–80% — SLO owner alerted, investigate root causes, schedule mitigation within 48h.
- Red: > 80% but < 100% — urgent mitigation, remove non-essential risky changes, schedule rollback if burn continues.
- Breach: >= 100% — trigger incident response, customer comms plan, pause risky deploys; SRE and product leaders to triage.

Canary and gating specifics:
- Canary must include SLO telemetry for its isolated traffic slice.
- Gate promotion requires no simulated SLO breach for 30m rolling window and error budget burn < 5% of monthly allowance.
- If the canary uses a new model variant, validate latency histogram shape and kv cache effects.

Dashboard and alert design patterns:
- Use histograms + heatmap for latency to expose distribution shifts.
- Display error-budget remaining as a single KPI on top.
- Use multi-window SLO charts (7d/30d) to reduce noisy short-term alerts.
- Alerting: two-tier alerts — alpha (paged to SRE) for Red zone and beta (email/Slack) for Yellow.

Runbooks and playbooks (integration):
- All runbooks must contain: immediate mitigation steps, rollback commands, customer impact assessment template, post-incident checklist.
- Consolidate into /confluence/sre/runbooks and tag by service.
- Add a short checklist card in the on-call rotation handoff deck.

Training and knowledge transfer:
- SRE will run two 60-minute workshops covering: reading SLO dashboards, interpreting error budget, basic remediation steps.
- Product owners must complete a 30-minute self-study and sign-off for routes they own.

Automation and CI/CD integration:
- Provide a helmfile template for routes deployed into k8s to include SLO manifest.
- GitHub action that validates SLO YAML against schema on PR.
- Canary job extension that queries metrics API and fails promotion if gating checks fail.

Observability costs and retention:
- Default: 14 days of high-resolution histograms, 90 days of aggregated SLO windows.
- Observability team to provide cost estimate per route before Phase 2 expansion.

Risks and mitigations:
- Metric drift (naming/label changes): mitigation — strict metric schema and CI validation.
- Alert fatigue: mitigation — multi-window smoothing and alert rate limiting.
- Ops capacity shortage during rollout: mitigation — staged rollout and temporary playbook simplifications.
- Customer communication mismatch: mitigation — involve CS early and create a pre-approved comms template.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Finalize per-tier SLOs for Dedicated customers vs Hosted. (Owner: Product, due Jul 18)
- Decide retention window for telemetry after the 14-day default for specific large routes. (Owner: Observability, due Aug 1)
- Confirm automated rollback thresholds for long-tail latency increases. (Owner: Serving runtime, due Jul 25)

Next steps (immediate):
1) PM sign-off on baseline SLO numbers (Sofia).
2) Infra change list for metric instrumentation (Lars).
3) Create pilot tickets: JIRA-2345, JIRA-2346, JIRA-2347 (pilot routes).
4) Schedule tabletop incident for Aug 11.

Appendix: quick checklist for a single route implementation
- [ ] SLO YAML checked into infra repo with schema pass.
- [ ] Metrics emitted and unit-tested.
- [ ] Dashboard tile exists and linked in the SLO YAML.
- [ ] Error budget policy doc uploaded and owner assigned.
- [ ] Runbook authored and attached to confluence.
- [ ] Canary gating configured in deployment pipeline.

Decision log snippets:
- 2025-07-09: Chose p99 for latency SLI over p90 due to customer sensitivity on tail latency. (Maya Chen)
- 2025-07-12: Agreed on 14d high-resolution retention default to control observability spend. (Imani Okafor)

Contact and escalation matrix:
- Primary SRE: maya@redwood.com
- Platform infra: lars@redwood.com
- Serving runtime: diego@redwood.com
- Product owner contact details documented in each route card.

This document is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight — use the templates referenced above and iterate. The goal for Q3 is repeatable pattern adoption rather than perfection for every single route.
